literal: Lekang County.
idiomatic: Lekang County.

literal: Attached to the prefectural seat.
idiomatic: It hugged the prefectural seat.

literal: Xingguo County.
idiomatic: Xingguo County.

literal: Originally people before the mountain; because of crime they were banished here and Xingzong established the county.
idiomatic: Originally upland people, banished here for crimes; Xingzong founded the county.

literal: Households 700.
idiomatic: 700 households.

literal: Changchun Prefecture, Shaoyang Army, lower grade, military commission.
idiomatic: Changchun Prefecture—Shaoyang Army, lower grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally the spring-hunt ground on the Yazi River.
idiomatic: Originally the Yazi River spring hunting grounds.

literal: Established in the eighth year of Xingzong Chongxi.
idiomatic: Founded in Xingzong's Chongxi year 8.

literal: Subordinate to Yanqing Palace; military affairs to the Northeast Commandery Army Office.
idiomatic: It belonged to Yanqing Palace; military affairs to the Northeast Commandery Army Office.

literal: It ruled one county: Changchun County.
idiomatic: It governed one county—Changchun County.

literal: Originally Hun Tong River land.
idiomatic: Originally Hun Tong River country.

literal: Criminals of Yan and Ji were exiled here.
idiomatic: Criminals from Yan and Ji were exiled here.

literal: Households 2,000.
idiomatic: 2,000 households.

literal: Wu Prefecture, Jing'an Army, cishi.
idiomatic: Wu Prefecture—Jing'an Army with a prefect.

literal: Originally Wuhuan land, a branch of the Eastern Hu.
idiomatic: Originally Wuhuan territory, an Eastern Hu branch.

literal: The Liao North Great King's Bala held it as pasture, built a city, later the state reclaimed it.
idiomatic: Liao North Great King Bala pastured here and walled a town; the state later reclaimed it.

literal: Subordinate to Xingsheng Palace.
idiomatic: It fell under Xingsheng Palace.

literal: There were Liao River, Ye River, Wuhuan River, and Wuhuan Mountain.
idiomatic: Waters included the Liao, Ye, and Wuhuan rivers; Wuhuan Mountain stood nearby.

literal: It ruled one county: Aimin County.
idiomatic: It governed one county—Aimin County.

literal: When Prince Bala campaigned south he captured Han people and placed them here.
idiomatic: Prince Bala, campaigning south, settled captured Han people here.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Yong Prefecture, Yongchang Army, surveillance commissioner.
idiomatic: Yong Prefecture—Yongchang Army with a surveillance commissioner.

literal: Built by Empress Chengtian.
idiomatic: Empress Chengtian founded it.

literal: Taizu here set up Nanlou.
idiomatic: Taizu established Nanlou here.

literal: In the third year of Qianheng a prefecture was set beside Prince Hanba's tomb.
idiomatic: Qianheng year 3 placed a prefecture beside Prince Hanba's tomb.

literal: East the Huang River, south the Tu River—the two waters joined, hence the name Yong Prefecture.
idiomatic: The Huang River lay east and the Tu River south; their confluence gave Yong Prefecture its name.

literal: In winter the royal camp often halted here, called the winter nabo.
idiomatic: Winter royal camps often halted here—the winter nabo.

literal: There was Muye Mountain with the Khitan Ancestor Temple; Qishou Khan in the south hall, Kedun in the north hall, painted images of the two sages and eight sons.
idiomatic: Muye Mountain held the Khitan Ancestor Temple—Qishou Khan in the south hall, Kedun in the north, with painted images of the two founders and their eight sons.

literal: Tradition says a divine man rode a white horse, floated down the Tu River from Mayu Mountain eastward; a heavenly woman drove a green ox cart from the Pingdi pine forest down the Huang River.
idiomatic: Legend tells of a god-man on a white horse floating down the Tu from Mayu Mountain, and a heavenly woman in a green ox cart descending the Huang from the Pingdi pine belt.

literal: At Muye Mountain the two waters met and they became spouses, bearing eight sons.
idiomatic: At Muye Mountain the rivers met; the pair wed and bore eight sons.

literal: Later the clan grew and divided into eight divisions.
idiomatic: Their clan later swelled and split into eight divisions.

literal: On every march and at spring and autumn sacrifices white horse and green ox were used to show they did not forget origins.
idiomatic: Every campaign and spring-autumn rite used a white horse and green ox so origins would not be forgotten.

literal: Xingwang Temple had a white-robed Guanyin image.
idiomatic: Xingwang Temple housed a white-robed Guanyin image.

literal: Taizong, aiding the Jin ruler to hold China, returning from Luzhou and entering Youzhou, visited Dabei Pavilion and pointed to this image saying: "I dreamed a god told me to send Lord Shi to rule China—this is he."
idiomatic: When Taizong helped the Jin ruler master China, returning from Luzhou through Youzhou he visited Dabei Pavilion and said of this image, "I dreamed a god bade me send Lord Shi to rule China—this is he."

literal: Therefore it was moved to Muye Mountain, a temple built, and spring and autumn offerings made, honored as the clan deity.
idiomatic: The image was moved to Muye Mountain, a temple raised, and spring and autumn rites made it the clan deity.

literal: Before raising armies they reported to it, then combined tally-arrows among the divisions.
idiomatic: Armies reported to it before marching, then combined tally-arrows across the divisions.

literal: There were also Gaodian Mountain and Willow Forest Marsh, also called White Horse Marsh.
idiomatic: Gaodian Mountain and Willow Forest Marsh—also called White Horse Marsh—lay nearby.

literal: Subordinate to Zhangmin Palace.
idiomatic: It belonged to Zhangmin Palace.

literal: It ruled three counties: Changning County.
idiomatic: It governed three counties—Changning County.

literal: Originally a county name of Xiande Prefecture.
idiomatic: Originally a county of Xiande Prefecture.

literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and moved its people here.
idiomatic: After Taizu pacified Bohai he resettled its people here.

literal: Households 4,500.
idiomatic: 4,500 households.

literal: Yifeng County.
idiomatic: Yifeng County.

literal: Originally Tieli Prefecture's Yi Prefecture.
idiomatic: Originally Yi Prefecture under Tieli Prefecture.

literal: When Liao troops broke it they moved the people northwest of Nanlou, still calling it Yi Prefecture.
idiomatic: Liao forces seized it and resettled the people northwest of Nanlou under the old name Yi Prefecture.

literal: In the first year of Chongxi the prefecture was abolished and the present county made.
idiomatic: Chongxi year 1 abolished the prefecture and created the present county.

literal: One hundred li northwest of the prefecture.
idiomatic: One hundred li northwest of the prefectural seat.

literal: It was once also changed to Fuyi County and belonged to Tai Prefecture.
idiomatic: It was once renamed Fuyi County and attached to Tai Prefecture.

literal: Beginnings and ends cannot be fully traced; both names now exist.
idiomatic: The full sequence cannot be recovered; both names survive in the record.

literal: Households 1,500.
idiomatic: 1,500 households.

literal: Ciren County.
idiomatic: Ciren County.

literal: Taizong, because Prince Zhisagu died, set Ci Prefecture west of the tomb.
idiomatic: After Prince Zhisagu's death Taizong placed Ci Prefecture west of his tomb.

literal: In the first year of Chongxi the prefecture was abolished and the present county made.
idiomatic: Chongxi year 1 abolished the prefecture and made the present county.

literal: Households 400.
idiomatic: 400 households.

literal: Yikun Prefecture, Qisheng Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Yikun Prefecture—Qisheng Army with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally land of the Khitan Right Great Division.
idiomatic: Originally territory of the Khitan Right Great Division.

literal: Empress Yingtian established the prefecture.
idiomatic: Empress Yingtian founded the prefecture.

literal: Uighur Nuosi dwelt there; to the fourth-generation grandson Rongwo Meili was born Empress Yingtian Shulü, who married Taizu.
idiomatic: Uighur Nuosi lived there; his fourth-generation descendant Rongwo Meili bore Empress Yingtian Shulü, who wed Taizu.

literal: Taizu opened the four directions and pacified Bohai; afterward she had great strength.
idiomatic: Taizu expanded on every side and pacified Bohai; afterward her influence was decisive.

literal: Captives with skills mostly entered her tent and were called Shushan.
idiomatic: Skilled captives mostly entered her tent and were called Shushan.

literal: A prefecture was set on her birthplace.
idiomatic: A prefecture was founded on her birthplace.

literal: The prefecture built Qisheng Hall; within Yining Hall held silver images of Taizu Heavenly Emperor and Empress Yingtian Earthly Empress.
idiomatic: Qisheng Hall stood in the prefecture; inside Yining Hall silver images of Taizu Heavenly Emperor and Empress Yingtian Earthly Empress.

literal: Subordinate to Changning Palace.
idiomatic: It belonged to Changning Palace.

literal: It ruled one county:
idiomatic: It governed one county:

literal: Guangyi County.
idiomatic: Guangyi County.

literal: Originally Uighur tribal pasture.
idiomatic: It had been Uighur tribal pasture.

literal: Empress Yingtian placed captives from the four campaigns here and therefore built prefecture and county.
idiomatic: Empress Yingtian settled captives from four campaigns here and founded prefecture and county.

literal: In the eighth year of Tonghe, households of the various palace supervisory offices were used to establish Laiyuan County; in the thirteenth year it was merged in.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 used palace supervisory households to found Laiyuan County; year 13 merged it into Guangyi.

literal: Households 2,500.
idiomatic: 2,500 households.

literal: Jiangsheng Prefecture, Kaiguo Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Jiangsheng Prefecture—Kaiguo Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally the land of the great tribal division's East Tower.
idiomatic: Originally the great tribal division's East Tower land.

literal: Taizu's spring traveling camp often halted here.
idiomatic: Taizu's spring camp often paused here.

literal: Empress Yingtian dreamed a god in gold crown and plain robes holding weapons, very handsome, with twelve strange beasts following.
idiomatic: Empress Yingtian dreamed a god in gold crown and plain robes bearing arms, strikingly handsome, with twelve strange beasts following.

literal: Among them a black hare leaped into her back and she conceived, then bore Taizong.
idiomatic: A black hare sprang into her back; she conceived and bore Taizong.

literal: Then black clouds covered the tent, firelight filled the chamber, thunder sounded, and the divisions were amazed.
idiomatic: Black clouds shrouded the tent, fire filled the chamber, thunder rolled, and the divisions marveled.

literal: Muzong established the prefecture.
idiomatic: Muzong founded the prefecture.

literal: On all four sides thirty li each, cutting firewood and grazing were forbidden.
idiomatic: Thirty li on every side forbade woodcutting and grazing.

literal: First subordinate to Yanchang Palace, later to Zhangmin Palace.
idiomatic: First under Yanchang Palace, later Zhangmin Palace.

literal: It ruled one county:
idiomatic: It governed one county:

literal: Yong'an County.
idiomatic: Yong'an County.

literal: Originally a county name of Longyuan Prefecture's Qing Prefecture.
idiomatic: The name came from a county of Longyuan Prefecture's Qing Prefecture.

literal: Taizu pacified Bohai, took Huai Prefecture's Yong'an, moved the people to settle in a stockade here, and built the county.
idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Bohai he seized Huai Prefecture's Yong'an, resettled its people in a stockade here, and founded the county.

literal: Households 800.
idiomatic: 800 households.

literal: Rao Prefecture, Kuangyi Army, middle grade, military commission.
idiomatic: Rao Prefecture—Kuangyi Army, middle grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally Tang Raole Prefecture land.
idiomatic: Originally Tang's Raole Prefecture territory.

literal: In Zhenguan Songmo Protectorate was set.
idiomatic: Zhenguan saw Songmo Protectorate established here.

literal: Taizu completed the old ramparts.
idiomatic: Taizu restored the old walls.

literal: There were Huang River, Changshui Marsh, Moda River, Qingshan, Dafu Mountain, and Song Mountain.
idiomatic: Landmarks included the Huang River, Changshui Marsh, Moda River, Qingshan, Dafu Mountain, and Song Mountain.

literal: Subordinate to Yanqing Palace.
idiomatic: It belonged to Yanqing Palace.

literal: It ruled three counties:
idiomatic: It governed three counties:

literal: Changle County.
idiomatic: Changle County.

literal: Originally a Liaocheng county name.
idiomatic: The name came from a Liaocheng county.

literal: Taizu attacked Bohai, moved its people, built a county, and settled them.
idiomatic: When Taizu attacked Bohai he resettled its people and founded Changle County.

literal: Households 4,000; within, 1,000 households paid iron tribute.
idiomatic: 4,000 households, including 1,000 paying iron tribute.

literal: Linhe County.
idiomatic: Linhe County.

literal: Originally people of Fengyong County; Taizong divided troops to attack Bohai and moved them to the bend of the Huang River.
idiomatic: Originally Fengyong County people; Taizong, campaigning against Bohai, resettled them on a Huang River bend.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Anmin County.
idiomatic: Anmin County.

literal: Taizong mixed captives from various Bohai settlements.
idiomatic: Taizong blended captives from several Bohai towns.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.
